headline: High-risk shared-filesystem pair: default workspace overlap enables prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write workspace files, and both support MCP. Claude Code shares state via filesystem and git; Continue shares state via filesystem and can ingest workspace files. That creates a default path where one agent’s file output can be treated as instructions by the other, even without a dedicated shared channel.
conditions: IF either agent writes attacker-controlled text into a shared workspace file
IF the other agent parses that file as instructions or tool input
mitigations: Separate the agents into different working directories
Disable MCP servers that expose untrusted file content
Use read-only mounts for one agent during review tasks
Add a manual review step before either agent consumes the other’s outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches git history, shell environment, and secrets such as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and git credentials, while Continue reads workspace files and open editor buffers. Because both share filesystem-based state, sensitive material can flow from A into B’s context or outputs in default coding workflows.
conditions: IF sensitive credentials or secrets are present in the shared workspace or shell environment
IF Continue opens files that Claude Code has written or modified
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared repo and shell history
Use separate OS users or separate worktrees
Redact credentials before either agent reads the workspace
Restrict Continue to a narrower folder than Claude Code
Rotate any exposed keys after joint sessions

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can execute shell commands, modify git state, and write files; Continue can write files and also shares state via filesystem. Even though Continue cannot run shell, both can mutate the same workspace, so concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt git state without coordination.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or directory at the same time
IF either agent writes files while the other is editing or committing
mitigations: Serialize access with a simple lock file
Assign one agent read-only access during the other’s write phase
Use separate branches for each agent
Run git status before and after each agent turn
Merge changes manually after both finish

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can produce code, patches, and shell-driven changes that Continue may then read from the workspace and act on. Continue’s tool use is MCP-based and user-approved, but its default workflow still consumes workspace content, so unverified outputs from A can cascade into B’s edits or recommendations.
conditions: IF Continue uses Claude Code’s written files as authoritative context
IF those files contain incorrect code, prompts, or patch instructions
mitigations: Require a human review of A’s output before B acts on it
Ask B to summarize and verify diffs instead of trusting them
Limit B to read-only analysis when consuming A’s artifacts
Keep generated artifacts in a separate staging directory

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are docs-only and there is no explicit residency or certification mismatch in the profiles. The main compliance concern is shared handling of secrets and workspace data, but the profiles do not show a specific regulated-data violation, so this remains a limited overlap risk rather than a breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace
IF either agent logs or persists that data beyond the intended session
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the shared repo
Check retention settings for any connected services
Use a scrubbed test dataset for joint runs
Delete temporary artifacts after the session
